question: Do symmetric additive collisions among three inherited Kummer radicals create unramified classes on high-jump fibres more often than on the frozen low-gain controls?
construction: For each unordered triple of generic x coordinates use q(theta)=(alpha_i+alpha_j-alpha_k)^2-4*alpha_i*alpha_j, alpha_i=x_i-theta. Clear rational scalar content to obtain a primitive integral quadratic q. The candidate is pi(q)=Norm(q)*q. Unlike multiplicative radical closure, this introduces addition.
incidence_gate: Remove from abs(Norm(q)) all factors supported on disc(f), by repeated gcd. A nonsquare remainder proves pi(q) ramified outside disc(f), because q is primitive and has degree below the cubic. A square remainder is only a necessary condition; it does not certify even ideal valuations, local solubility or independence.
inputs: All sixteen frozen masked equations and their marked generic sections. No exceptional points, rank labels, new parameters or selected triples derived from outcomes.
controls: Apply the same norm gate to every inherited linear Kummer representative and to f'(theta). The latter projects to the derivative class already excluded from Selmer, so it is a deliberate false-positive control for this necessary gate.
failure: A zero norm or degenerate polynomial is reported separately. Surviving candidates remain UNKNOWN until exact ideal valuations, complete local conditions and independence are established. This is not a rank score or point visibility test.
